data.narrative:
The Nuclear Company is a Series A-stage nuclear energy venture that has raised $50M+. The broader nuclear energy sector includes 3 public comparables (OKLO, NNE, SMR) and 8 private peers, including later-stage companies such as Fuse Energy, X-Energy, and Oklo.

Stage-progression analysis is the applicable valuation method here. Using total capital raised ($50M) as a proxy for post-money valuation at Series A entry, a 2.0x step-up multiplier—consistent with typical Series A to growth-stage progression—implies a valuation of $100M. This method anchors the analysis directly to observed funding patterns within the frontier nuclear sector.

Peer-median comparison is not reliable given insufficient narrow-peer density. While four nuclear energy companies exist in the comp universe, only one occupies the same stage and one an adjacent stage; the narrow filters (same-stage, similar tier) do not yield three or more datapoints necessary for statistical credibility. Broadening to all-sector medians would obscure stage and maturity differences material to valuation.

The triangulated range supported by applicable methods is $85M (low) to $115M (high), with $100M as the median point. Key uncertainties include commercialization timeline, regulatory pathway clarity, and capital intensity to deployment—factors not yet fully reflected in single-method output. A second valuation method would meaningfully strengthen conviction in this range.
